messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: How software R can read an accent while working in French?
parts:
Hi Mouna,

as mentioned by previous posters, this isn't exactly ggplot2 issue. It's not entirely an R issue, either. Keep in mind that displaying things in R may differ to what is written to a file. I whole heatedly sympathise with you and wish you best of luck.

You should keep in mind that what you see in R (correct/incorrect characters) depends on at least three factors (I hope I get the technicalities more or less correct). One is how the file is written. Sometimes encoding of the file is "weird" which can cause some headaches downstream. Second thing is how you read the data into R. If the encoding argument in your function that reads the file doesn't match the codepage in the file, you will get erratic results. Third, R displays characters based on encoding set in the options (Sys.getlocale()). If the set codepage doesn't support the displayed character, you're more or less out of luck. To add an extra layer of complication, R displays text based on encoding based on what system has (as default), and this differs from OS to OS.

Questions about this are tumbleweeds on Stackoverflow, possibly because a lot of developers don't bother with this, if they work with encoding UTF-8.

If your OS allows it, I would set R encoding to UTF-8, change file encoding (if possible) to UTF-8 and use functions that take the encoding argument. That way, you are almost guaranteed to see all the characters read, displayed and written correctly.

Cheers,
Roman
